question: In the ATLAS measurement of lepton distributions in ttbar events at 8 TeV, what fraction of the observed one-b-tag events is estimated to be background?
expect: 2,630 / 21,666 = 12.1% (Table 2, p5); consistent with the ~88% purity in the text
rendered:
The text does not explicitly state the fraction of observed one-b-tag events that is estimated to be background. However, it does provide the estimated background contributions to the one-b-tag events, which are listed in Table 2 as follows:

- Wt single top: 2080 ± 210 events (about 9.6% of the total one-b-tag events)
- Z(→ ττ → eμ)+jets: 210 ± 40 events (about 0.98% of the total one-b-tag events)
- Diboson: 120 ± 30 events (about 0.56% of the total one-b-tag events)
- Misidentified leptons: 220 ± 80 events (about 1.03% of the total one-b-tag events)
- Total background: 2630 ± 230 events (about 12.3% of the total one-b-tag events)

Note that the total background fraction is not explicitly stated in the text, but it can be estimated by summing the background contributions and dividing by the total number of one-b-tag events (21666).
